title: Foundations: Bebop Vocal - The Complete Guide
summary: What Bebop Vocal is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Bebop Vocal songs: Bebop vocals ride the fastest changes in jazz: singers scat-syllable their way through bebop heads at breakneck tempo, matching the horns note for note. Ella Fitzgerald turned scat into high art.

History: Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker invented bebop in 1940s after-hours sessions. Ella Fitzgerald's scat choruses, and later Jon Hendricks's vocalese (words written to recorded solos), defined the vocal art.

How the songs work: Bebop Vocal favors the keys of Bb, F, C, Eb. Common forms include Head–scat solos–head at 200+ bpm; Vocalese: lyrics set to famous solos. Players should master scat syllables: doo-bop-shoo-be-doo-be-doo first, then double-time lines over walking bass. Instrumental keys; scat needs no capo.
facts: Bebop vocals ride the fastest changes in jazz: singers scat-syllable their way through bebop heads at breakneck tempo, matching the horns note for note. Ella Fitzgerald turned scat into high art.

Typical keys: Bb, F, C, Eb
Core technique: Double-time lines over walking bass

# Bebop Vocal foundations
# Key of Bb - Bebop blues
CHART = [
    "A#",
    "D#",
    "A#",
    "A#",
    "D#",
    "D#",
    "A#",
    "A#",
    "Cm",
    "F7",
    "A#",
    "F7",
]
KEY = "Bb"

NOTES=['C','C#','D','D#','E','F','F#','G','G#','A','A#','B']
FLAT={'Db':'C#','Eb':'D#','Gb':'F#','Ab':'G#','Bb':'A#'}
import re
def _semi(k):
    m=re.match(r'^([A-G][#b]?)',k); r=FLAT.get(m.group(1),m.group(1))
    return NOTES.index(r)
def transpose(ch, steps):
    m=re.match(r'^([A-G][#b]?)(.*)$',ch)
    r=FLAT.get(m.group(1),m.group(1))
    return NOTES[(NOTES.index(r)+steps)%12]+m.group(2)
def to_key(chords, target):
    steps=(_semi(target)-_semi(chords[0]))%12
    return [transpose(c,steps) for c in chords]

print('Original chart (key of '+KEY+'):')
for i in range(0,len(CHART),4):
    print('  '+' | '.join(CHART[i:i+4]))
print()
print('Transposed to G:')
tr=to_key(CHART,'G')
for i in range(0,len(tr),4):
    print('  '+' | '.join(tr[i:i+4]))

title: A Night in Tunisia - Bebop Vocal Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for A Night in Tunisia by Dizzy Gillespie (1942).
body:
A Night in Tunisia — Dizzy Gillespie, 1942. The bebop national anthem.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of Bb):
A# | D# | A# | A#
D# | D# | A# | A#
Cm | F7 | A# | F7

This study chart uses the 'Bebop blues' progression, the Bebop Vocal workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: head–scat solos–head at 200+ bpm. Listen for double-time lines over walking bass — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Bebop Vocal pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let double-time lines over walking bass. Instrumental keys; scat needs no capo. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
facts: Technique focus: Double-time lines over walking bass

program.code:
# A Night in Tunisia study
# Key of Bb - Bebop blues
CHART = [
    "A#",
    "D#",
    "A#",
    "A#",
    "D#",
    "D#",
    "A#",
    "A#",
    "Cm",
    "F7",
    "A#",
    "F7",
]
KEY = "Bb"

NOTES=['C','C#','D','D#','E','F','F#','G','G#','A','A#','B']
FLAT={'Db':'C#','Eb':'D#','Gb':'F#','Ab':'G#','Bb':'A#'}
import re
def _semi(k):
    m=re.match(r'^([A-G][#b]?)',k); r=FLAT.get(m.group(1),m.group(1))
    return NOTES.index(r)
def transpose(ch, steps):
    m=re.match(r'^([A-G][#b]?)(.*)$',ch)
    r=FLAT.get(m.group(1),m.group(1))
    return NOTES[(NOTES.index(r)+steps)%12]+m.group(2)
def to_key(chords, target):
    steps=(_semi(target)-_semi(chords[0]))%12
    return [transpose(c,steps) for c in chords]

print('Original chart (key of '+KEY+'):')
for i in range(0,len(CHART),4):
    print('  '+' | '.join(CHART[i:i+4]))
print()
print('Transposed to G:')
tr=to_key(CHART,'G')
for i in range(0,len(tr),4):
    print('  '+' | '.join(tr[i:i+4]))
